Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid)

Feast of St. Muirgen: A Day by the Sea

Celebrate the legend of Lí Ban, the mermaid of Lough Neagh, by honoring her story and the coastal traditions of Ireland with a day of reflection, nature, and a special seafood feast.

  1. Morning

    Read the Tale of Lí Ban

    Begin your day by reading the story of Lí Ban from the Annals of the Four Masters to connect with her journey from the bursting of Lough Neagh to her transformation and baptism as St. Muirgen.

  2. Late Morning

    Walk by the Water

    Take a reflective walk along a local shore or body of water, imagining the shores of Lough Neagh or Larne Lough, to honor Lí Ban’s connection to the sea and those who live by it.

  3. Midday

    Light a Candle for Sailors

    Light a candle in a window or on your table as a symbol of hope and protection for sailors and all who depend on the sea, continuing a tradition of remembrance and blessing.

  4. Afternoon

    Prepare the Coastal Feast

    Begin preparing a coastal-inspired meal featuring traditional Irish seafood and breads to celebrate the bounty of the sea and Lí Ban’s legacy.

    Recipes: Poached Irish Salmon · Dulse and Carrageen Pudding · Bangor Oysters · Brown Soda Bread with Salted Butter

  5. Evening

    Feast in Honor of St. Muirgen

    Gather around the table to enjoy poached Irish salmon, dulse and carrageen pudding, fresh Bangor oysters, and brown soda bread with salted butter, accompanied by tea or a measure of Bushmills whiskey.

    Recipes: Poached Irish Salmon · Dulse and Carrageen Pudding · Bangor Oysters · Brown Soda Bread with Salted Butter · Traditional Brewed Tea · Bushmills Irish Whiskey Cocktail

  6. After Dinner

    Share Stories and Reflections

    Conclude your day by sharing stories or reflections about the sea, transformation, and faith, keeping the spirit of Lí Ban alive in your home.

End your day with gratitude for the sea’s gifts and the enduring legend of St. Muirgen, carrying her story in your heart until next year.

Feast-day recipes

  • Poached Irish Salmon
  • Dulse and Carrageen Pudding
  • Bangor Oysters
  • Brown Soda Bread with Salted Butter
  • Traditional Brewed Tea
